chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī and Abū Qatādah, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who comes upon water in a streamlet or a pond: may he perform ghusl for janabah in it, or perform wudu (ablution) from it for salat (prayer), when he finds no other than it, while the water does not amount to a sāʿ for janabah nor to a mudd for wudu (ablution), and it is scattered? So how should he use it, while fearing that beasts may have drunk from it?

He said: "If his hand is clean, then let him take a handful of water with one hand and sprinkle it behind him, and a handful in front of him, and a handful to his right, and a handful to his left. If he fears that it will not suffice him, he should wash his head three times, then wipe his skin with his hand, for that will suffice him. And if it is wudu (ablution), he should wash his face and pass his hand over his forearms, his head, and his feet. If the water is scattered and he is able to gather it, then he should gather it; otherwise, he should perform ghusl from this and that. If it is in one place and it is little, not enough for his ghusl, then there is no problem in his performing ghusl and returning the water into it, for that will suffice him."

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.سَاقِيَةٍ: a small flowing watercourse or streamlet
key_terms.مَسَحَ: he wiped or passed the hand over
key_terms.مُتَفَرِّقٌ: scattered or dispersed in separate places
key_terms.مُسْتَنْقَعٍ: a pond or stagnant collection of water

ai.seo_question: How should someone perform ghusl or wudu (ablution) when only a small scattered amount of water is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the use of a small amount of water for ghusl and wudu (ablution) when no other water is available. It explains practical procedures for ritual purification in cases of scarcity and dispersed water, showing the flexibility of the law in preserving taharah and enabling worship.
